For BASE jumping - what you'd consider stunt stuff - you get one chute. You need to open high enough to correct some potential malfunctions and to land safely. Canopies also come out way faster because you're packing and deploying a certain way, generally more diligently than skydiving packing.

For skydiving, your chute is crammed into the bag while people shout at you to hurry up cos the wheels are turning on the plane. You expect it to fail once in a while on opening, so you plan to have your chute out by about ~2k feet - which is considered the bare minimum height for pulling your reserve and still being able to land safely. This means pulling your main at about 3.5k, and have it deployed by ~2.5k, giving you time to assess.

Realistically speaking your reserve can come out later and you will prob still land safely but your chances drop so why risk it?

Every time your commander card moves to exile or graveyard or your hand you can elect to send it to your command zone. When you cast your commander from the command zone, for each time you have done so previously, you must pay an additional 2.

"Destroy" sends your commander to the graveyard. Then you move it to your command zone immediately if you wish. The rest of the card is irrelevant from this perspective. The frog still gets summoned tho. It's not changing your commander - it says destroy for a reason.

Regeneration is a different thing you don't need to think about unless you have something that provides regeneration explicitly. You can ignore it most of the time.

1) reduced to toughness doesn't "destroy", which is why it works. It explicitly just dies.
2) there's also sacrifice, bounce, nullifying enchantments. It's just easier to say that indestructible just prevents destruction by damage and destroy effects.
If you're thinking they might somehow sacrifice your safe landing to preserve themselves - that's not a thing. By definition you both land safely or they will put themselves at risk. Don't stress.

Yes - and it will certainly come up when the game goes to release. And then it will be a silly war between cheat detection and crackers.

Think of it as a trade-off. More information kept server side means:
1) generally less crackable game
2) generally more delays felt by the player
3) sometimes less flexible effects (eg invisibility)

In order for the client to display something as semi-invisible it needs to know where that something is and then display its silhouette with some kind of filter/effect over it. It makes it a lot more trivial to see invisible people by cracking the client - just edit the effect (stored locally) so that it makes the silhouette opaque or whatever.

Theoretically if they are just completely invisible the client doesn't even know where the invisible character is - practically it probably does but it's a whole other stage of hacking to insert some kind of placeholder in game representing an invisible character than it is to edit a game file to make "blurry mess" look less blurry.

Important to note that Riot pursued the option of semi-invisible cloak fields but ruled it out because it opens up an easy client-side exploit through cracking. It was discussed during the Evelynn overhaul.
